No, mass drug administration (MDA) alone is unlikely to lead to the sustainable control of schistosomiasis. While MDA can significantly reduce the prevalence and intensity of infection in the short term, it may not address the underlying environmental and socioeconomic factors that contribute to the persistence of the disease. 

Repeated MDA campaigns can lead to rebound infections, as the parasite can survive in the environment and reinfect treated individuals. Additionally, MDA may exert selective pressure on the parasite population, potentially leading to the development of drug resistance.

A more sustainable approach to controlling schistosomiasis involves a multi-faceted strategy that includes MDA, as well as improvements in water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) infrastructure, health education, and snail control measures. This integrated approach can help to reduce the transmission of the disease and ultimately achieve long-term control and potential elimination of schistosomiasis.
